newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to receive Russian gas at lower prices.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to receive Russian gas at lower prices.

text.p: Bulgaria will receive up to 115 billion cubic metres natural gas from Russia in the next 15 years at lower prices under the terms of a draft intergovernmental agreement, officials said on Wednesday.

Bulgargas executive director Vasil Filipov said the agreement between the two countries for Russian gas supplies to Bulgaria, transiting Russian gas to the Balkans and construction of new transiting pipelines envisages costs at $99.99 per 1,000 cubic metres.

"Up to now we received Russian natural gas at the Bulgarian border (with Romania) at the price of some $107.5 per 1,000 cubic metres and with the Value Added Tax, duty fees and other taxes the price was going up to $150 per 1,000 cubic metres," Filipov said.
Filipov said the interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski and Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin are due to sign the intergovernmental agreement on Friday in Moscow.
Bulgaria's and Russian officials on Tuesday agreed the terms of the long-delayed pact, turning Bulgaria into a centre in the Balkans for distributing Russian natural gas.
Bulgaria has a 2,200-km pipeline network, including 625 km of transit pipelines which receive and transmit gas from outside the country.

But a Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy, half-owned by Russia's RAO Gazprom and assigned by Gazprom to build new pipelines in Bulgaria, needs to enlarge the transit pipeline and compressor stations to meet the growing Balkan demand.

Filipov told a news conference that Bulgargas would receive 60 percent from the transiting fees and the remaining 40 pecent would go to pay Topenergy for constructing new pipelines, which would be state-owned.

Bulgargas is now negotiating commercial contracts with Topenergy for the construction of transiting pipelines and transiting Russian gas through Bulgarian territory to Turkey, Greece, Macedonia and Serbia.

Topenergy will fund the pipelines' construction with credits from Gazprom, Filipov said, adding that Bulgargas would not participate in financing construction works after it had built new pipelines to Macedonia and Greece.
Construction of a second pipeline between the Bulgarian borders with Romania and Turkey is expected to start next year, officials said.
For the last nine years a gas pipeline has linked Bulgaria with Turkey, but Gazprom hopes to boost its exports to Turkey to 30 billion cubic metres (bcm) from some 6.5 bcm.
Bulgaria's gas monopoly is also negotiating another contract with a private gas firm Overgas Inc, also half-owned by Gazprom, for Russian gas supplies to Bulgaria.
"All contracts are expected to be signed in 2-3 days," Filipov said.
